sentences.text: Mioaetus is an extinct genus of accipitrids, a group that includes modern eagles and hawks, whose name means “Miocene eagle.”
The type locality for the genus is the Hammerschmiede clay pit in southern Germany.
Fossils of Mioaetus were discovered in Germany.
The genus was formally described by Gerald Mayr, Thomas Lechner, and Madelaine Böhme.
Mioaetus lived during the Miocene epoch.
The taxon is currently regarded as valid.
The type species assigned to the genus is Mioaetus pforzenensis.
The Hammerschmiede site preserved a productive river system that likely offered abundant fish and other prey for piscivorous birds such as Mioaetus.
Mioaetus belongs to the family Accipitridae, which contains most birds of prey such as eagles, hawks, and kites.
Only a single species, M. pforzenensis, is known from the genus.
Fossils date to the early Late Miocene, specifically the earliest Tortonian stage, from southern Germany.
